appendix.title: Procmail recipes
appendix.para: The first line of a procmail filter always starts with “:0” and the remaining letters controls the filtering process.

For example “h” will only filter on the mail headers, “c” will make a copy of the mail so that it is available to filters after the current filter. If there is no “c” then the filter will consume the mail and processing stops here and no more filters will be applied to the mail.

sect1.title: The problem of filtering on the “Subject:” field
sect1.para: While at first it might seem simple enough to filter out certain mails with a specific subject either as spam or some other reason it is in practice a lot more complicated. The problem is that the subject does not always have to be in plain text. Instead it is very common to have the subject in either quoted printable or in base64. Such an encoded string looks like =?charset?format?encoded text?= (this format is more specifically described in RFC1522) and it can also be followed by some text in plain format and then again by some encoded text. For obvious reason a lot of spam uses this format to make it much more difficult to do simple text matching.
Unfortunately there is no easy way around this and procmail does not have any built in “decoding” functionality so this has to be done manually.

To help with this the following small perl script can be used as a helper script. This script has been floated on the net and the author is unfortunately unknown to me (if you know please let me now and the proper credit will be given)

sect1.title: How to create filter that matches on any of several rules (creating an “OR” rule)
sect1.para: By default all matching rules in a filter need to apply before the action is taken. To create a rule which simulates an “OR” condition for the matching expression one has to make use of the “else” rule. This is done by executing an empty action “{ }” when all the conditions do NOT match and our “real” actions if this condition is not true. (This uses the fact that NOT( (NOT A) AND (NOT B)) = A OR B )

para.emphasis: Please note that there should be one space in the “{ }” empty statement!

sect1.title: Out of office
sect1.para: The following receipe shows how to send an automatic answer to incoming messages. Fro this we use the utility program "formmail". We also take some precaution to avoid an infinite loop when the sender also have an automatic reply to avoid mails just bouncing back and forth.
sect1.programlisting: #-------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Out of office #-------------------------------------------------------------------------- :0 h c * !^FROM_DAEMON * !^FROM_MAILER * !^X-Loop: out_of_office | (/usr/bin/formail -r -A"Precedence: junk (autoreply)" -A"X-Loop: out_of_office" \ -I"Subject: Out of office reply"; cat $HOME/out_of_office.txt) | $SENDMAIL -t

sect1.title: Replying with a mail based on subject
sect1.para: This shows how to use formmail to perform an action based on the subject of an incoming mail. In this particular case we respond to a specific mail by powering on a remote server
sect1.programlisting: #--------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Sending a reply based on subject #--------------------------------------------------------------------------- :0 h c * ^Subject: gwake | (/usr/bin/formail -r -I"Subject: Server gamma waking up (autoreply)" ; \ echo "This is not a guarant\ ee that the server has woken up though. " ) | $SENDMAIL -t

sect1.title: A template to start with
sect1.para: The final example is not really an example but a template that you may use to get a good start in writing your own rules. It give a logical structure and establishes some "best practices" to get readable and understandable procmail files (as far as that is possible). This template will give you

listitem.para: A logfile under /tmp for each month
Spamfiltering based on spamassassin with both filtering to a "Spam" folder and also direct deletion of mails with a high spam score (>=15)
A good practice of giving symbolic names to the mail folders where to store mail

sect1.programlisting:
#--------------------------------------------- # Standard setup for extra logging #--------------------------------------------- VERBOSE=on LOGABSTRACT=all LOGFILE=/tmp/procmail-${LOGNAME}-`date +%Y%m`.log
#--------------------------------------------- # Some standard paths #--------------------------------------------- MAILDIR=/srv/mail/${LOGNAME} DEFAULT=${MAILDIR}/ INBOX=${MAILDIR}/
#--------------------------------------------- # Subfolders to store mails in. You should add # a variable for each folder you are using in your # mail setup. The wasiest way to create the proper # folders is to do it via you email client, # REMEMBER TO PUT TRAILING '/' AT THE END # to mark that the folders are in maildir format. #--------------------------------------------- SPAM=${MAILDIR}/.Junk/ NEWSLETTERS=${MAILDIR}/.newsletters/
##-------------------------------------------- ## End of setup. Now comes all the filer ## rules. ##--------------------------------------------
#--------------------------------------------- # FILTER all Newsletters. #--------------------------------------------- :0 ^Subject:.*Newsletter ^From:.*news.com { } :0 E $NEWSLETTERS
#--------------------------------------------- # FILTER for spamassassin. Only run mails smaller than ½ MB # through spamassassin #--------------------------------------------- :0 * < 512000 | /usr/bin/spamc
#--------------------------------------------- # Delete all spams with score >= 15 #--------------------------------------------- :0 * !^X-Spam-Level: \*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*\*.* * !^X-Spam-Status: Yes, score=1[5-9]\.[0-9] * !^X-Spam-Status: Yes, score=[2-9][0-9]\.[0-9] { } :0 E /dev/null
#--------------------------------------------- # Put all remaining identified spams in Junk folder. # NOTE: This assumes spamassassin is configured to # set the X-Spam-Flag: YES for identified spams. #--------------------------------------------- :0 * ^X-Spam-Flag: YES $SPAM
#--------------------------------------------- # Store the reaming mails to the inbox #--------------------------------------------- :0 $DEFAULT
